question: on sequence outside the 882 real-unknown blocks, how often does a GTEx v8 fine-mapped cis-eQTL name the gene a CRISPRi screen measured an element to regulate, how often at matched windows, how clustered are its hits, and how many blocks would a test of the blocks' attribution need?
what_an_eqtl_is: an association between a variant and a gene's expression across people; not a perturbation and not mechanism. Fine-mapping localises the association to a variant with a posterior; it does not say which element acts
fair_test_rule: Fixed in the committed code before the calibration is run. A test inside the blocks is registered only if, at the calibrated rates and at the scale the test would use, BOTH hold for the blocks available to it (those whose attribution names a gene whose TSS lies on the same chromosome within the 1 Mb cis window and outside the unit): (1) the conditional test reaches 80% probability of detection at one-sided alpha 0.05 when half of the attributions are right and the rest behave as matched windows (f = 1/2); and (2) when none is right but the blocks behave as CRISPRi-tested elements that do not regulate the named gene, it rejects at most twice the nominal level (0.10), so the matched-window control is not fooled by sequence of the kind a screen tests. If neither scale meets both, no test is registered and the reason is recorded with the numbers. The rule reads the sizing table and the count of available blocks, nothing else.
window_design: four control windows and one pseudo-block per unit, within a quarter of the unit's distance to the TSS (at least three unit lengths) and a quarter of its common-variant count. A design probe that read coordinates and common-variant counts only, before any eQTL value, found that ten disjoint windows in a tenth-wide band fit around under half of the positives at the element scale and about a tenth at the block scale, the losses near the TSS
incidental_reads: the held-track test as committed in 68a273b decoded chr21's DAP-G records outside chr21:30-35 Mb only, so it decoded the records of chr21's five real-unknown blocks as well, and asserted only that every PIP lies in [0, 1] and that Whole_Blood is among the chromosome's tissues; nothing was printed, counted or kept. 16a415f narrowed it to chr21:18-22 Mb, inside a gap between two blocks

a design probe before 68a273b read only coordinates and dbSNP common-variant counts (no eQTL value) to choose the number of windows and the bands; exploration printed DAP-G records only from outside the widened blocks

superseded_first_run.what_was_wrong: the sizing's window null always took the FIRST drawn window as the pseudo-block and the other four as its controls. That window hit more often than the rest among the positives (0.0323 against 0.0242 at the element scale, 0.0723 against 0.0477 at the block scale), a gap the resampling then treated as real, so with no attribution right the test rejected more as blocks were added (0.36 of experiments at 882 blocks at the element scale, 0.91 at the block scale) and power rose as the share right FELL. The window null was not calibrated. It now chooses the pseudo-block at random among the five windows in every simulated block, and a right block's controls are four of its five windows chosen at random; the window rate is the mean over all five
superseded_first_run.what_did_not_change: the units, windows, flanks, hits and every rate at the units; the tested-negative null (its no-attribution rejection rate stayed at or under 0.0255 at every size)
superseded_first_run.its_decision: no fair test at either scale: at the element scale 285 available blocks gave 0.197 probability of detection at f = 1/2; at the block scale 179 gave 0.273

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 63e91d3

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
